name: showreel-34-press

voice.text: Why does your button feel dead on tap? You tap. Nothing moves. So you tap again. The fix: while it's pressed, scale it to ninety six percent and drop the shadow. Watch it slowed down. It sinks, the shadow drops, then it springs back. Now every tap feels real.

caption:
Why does your button feel dead on tap? 👆

With no :active style, a tap gives no sign it landed, so people tap again (and pay twice). While the button is pressed, shrink it to 96%, drop its shadow and darken it a touch, with a 0.12 s transition: it sinks under the finger and springs back. On iPhone, Safari only shows :active when the page listens for touches, so add ontouchstart to your <body>. scale works in Chrome 104+, Safari 14.1+ and Firefox 72+ (or use transform: scale(.96) for older browsers).
Save it for your next button, or send it to whoever built your checkout.

sources.note: MDN :active: matches an element while it is being activated (pressed) by the user; BCD css.selectors.active: all browsers; safari_ios note: by default Safari on iOS does not use :active unless there is a touchstart handler on the element or on <body> (read from mdn/browser-compat-data 12 Nov 2026)
MDN scale (the individual transform property); BCD css.properties.scale: Chrome 104, Firefox 72, Safari 14.1 (iOS mirror)

tip.title: Why does your button feel dead on tap?
tip.why: A button with no :active style gives no sign a tap landed, so people tap again. A short transition plus scale: .96, a collapsed box-shadow and a slight brightness drop while :active make it sink under the finger and spring back (MDN :active, scale). Safari on iOS only applies :active when the page has a touchstart listener, so add ontouchstart to <body> (BCD note).
